The trace is not impaired for policy purposes, so the deviation stands on it alone. It carries 131 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval with 100.0% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds: it shows no gap above 90 seconds under POL-RD-07(a), no straight-line jump above 500 m under POL-RD-07(b) and no sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds under POL-RD-07(c). Billed distance equals traced distance, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall in the driver's favour to be netted either, and every ledger line is accounted for by distance, time, base fare and platform fee.

The $13.68 refund is 63.7% of charged_total (13.68 / 21.48), short of the 90% share at which POL-RD-02 substitutes FULL_REFUND for a partial, so the ceiling on this record is a PARTIAL_REFUND of the contested amount and the rider's asserted $21.48 is not attainable on any line.

No repeat-deviation uplift is open on this trip. POL-RD-06's pattern test runs on two fields and no others — driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d — and the driver's profile shows 0 deviation flags across 210 completed trips in the trailing 90 days: 0 is below the 3-flag limb and 0.00 is below the 0.05 ratio limb, so no pattern is established, the POL-RD-02 partial is not uplifted to a FULL_REFUND of charged_total, and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is a near-synonym of deviation_flags_90d and is context only under POL-GEN-01; I do not rely on it.

Nothing is added to the distance-and-time figure. The fare_breakdown carries no ERP or toll charge at all — the on-optimal-route and off-optimal-route totals are both $0.00 and erp_gantries is empty — and in any event POL-RD-09(1) provides that off-route ERP is already comprehended in a POL-RD-02 refund and must never be stacked on top of it, so the pass-through correction for this trip is nil.

The driver's account is on file — that the rider changed the destination verbally — and I do not stretch it beyond what the record can carry. POL-RD-04 requires an instruction recorded in the chat_log for this trip and corroborated against chat_message.waypoint_hint, and the chat_log records no message at all (EV-CHAT-02824, weight 1.0, 0 messages); POL-RD-05 requires an amended endpoint and the stored amended optimal, and the trip record shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at null with amended_optimal_distance_km null, a figure the tribunal is forbidden to derive. Neither clause can exclude any distance on this record, so the excess is measured against the booked 2.4 km optimal route — although the empty chat log neither contradicts the driver's account nor corroborates the rider's.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver, in plain language.

WHAT THE RECORD SHOWS. Trip TRP-02824 is the same trip on all three instruments — trip record, GPS trace and fare breakdown — and the trace's first fix (2026-08-29T16:11:03+08:00) matches the recorded trip_started event. Under POL-RD-01 the governing distance field is gps_trace.trace_distance_km on EV-GPS-02824: 14.4 km. The booked optimal on EV-TRIP-02824 is 2.4 km, so the excess is 12.0 km — 500% of optimal and far above the 0.8 km absolute floor. Both establishment limbs pass, and because the excess also exceeds 50% of optimal and 8.0 km, this is additionally a MATERIAL deviation, which is why the driver's profile was checked.

TRACE INTEGRITY. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: 131 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 s. None of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is met, so no independent corroboration under POL-RD-07(ii) is required and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. The rider's duration point (21.7 min actual against a 5.0 min platform estimate) is consistent with the trace, but distance is decided on the trace figure as POL-RD-01 requires.

THE DRIVER'S EXPLANATION. You say the rider changed the destination verbally. POL-RD-04 exonerates a detour only where the rider's instruction is recorded in the chat_log, is timestamped before the vehicle left the optimal corridor (or no more than 3 minutes after) and is corroborated by the trace against chat_message.waypoint_hint. EV-CHAT-02824 is present and complete at weight 1.0, but it holds zero messages: no instruction is recorded, no timestamp exists to test, and the 200 m corroboration test cannot be run. The clause is therefore unavailable, and your account cannot stand in for the chat log because POL-RD-04 names the log as its test, not a party statement. Under POL-RD-08 your assertion points to no artifact that carries it and discharges nothing. POL-RD-05 does not apply either: no pickup or dropoff amendment timestamp is present and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so there is no re-quote to re-apply. POL-RD-12 does not apply: the vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so the baseline stays the booked 2.4 km optimal.

NO TRAFFIC EXONERATION. The only advisory, EV-ADVIS-02824-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; it can carry no fact, and its absence is what is cited. No closure-adjusted optimal exists, so no distance is excluded on that ground.

THE REFUND ARITHMETIC (POL-RD-02, fare_model METERED). charged_total is $21.48 on EV-FARE-02824. recomputed_fare = (($3.80 base + $0.75 x 2.4 optimal km + $0.28 x 5.0 optimal min) x 1.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + $0.80 platform fee + $0.00 ERP and tolls + $0.00 fixed surcharges + $0.00 waiting time - $0.00 promo = $7.80. Refund = $21.48 - $7.80 = $13.68, rounded up to the nearest $0.05, giving $13.70. That is 63.7% of charged_total — below the 90% share at which POL-RD-02 substitutes a full refund, and far above the $0.50 de minimis floor. The rider's demand for the whole $21.48 is therefore not attainable. No ERP or toll line exists on the ledger, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing and the anti-double-count rule has nothing to correct.

NO DRIVER COMPENSATION. The billed distance of 14.4 km equals the traced distance, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall over 1.0 km and the POL-RD-04 compensation limb is not met. Your charge for the distance actually billed stands; the refund corrects only the excess over the optimal route.

DRIVER PROFILE CHECK (POL-RD-06). deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 210 completed_trips_90d. Neither limb is met (0 is below 3; 0/210 is below the 0.05 ratio), so no repeat pattern is established: the POL-RD-02 partial is not uplifted to a full refund, and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is a near-synonym that POL-GEN-01 makes context only, and it was not used. Symmetrically, the rider's deviation_claims_60d of 1 (0 substantiated) does not raise the corroboration bar under POL-RD-08. Rating, account age, lifetime trips and cancellation rates on either profile were not used as grounds.

OUTCOME. Part of the contested amount is returned: PARTIAL_REFUND of $13.70 to the rider. Because that figure exceeds the $8.00 execution threshold, the ruling issues but the amount is held for human release under POL-GEN-05 rather than executed automatically; this is not an escalation and no clause produces a referral here. Under POL-GEN-04 either party may appeal once within 30 days.
